Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:10:1.english: He sold him a house - and [the buyer] gave him all of its value.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:10:2.hebrew: ואמר לו - מוכר, ע"מ כן אני מוכר לך, שכשיהיו לי מעות, החזירם לי וטול מעותיך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:10:2.english: And he said to him - [The] seller [said to him:] On this condition I am selling to you, that when I have money, return them [the house or field] to me and take your money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:10:3.hebrew: אסור - דנמצא שאין זה מכר, וכשאכל פירות, שכר מעותיו עומד ונוטל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:10:3.english: [It is] prohibited - For it turns out that this is not a [true] sale, and when he consumed [the] produce, he ends up taking compensation for his money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:10:4.english: When you have money, I will return them to you - The buyer said this to him of his own accord.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:10:5.english: Permitted - And later [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:10:6.english: Who taught [this] - [It] refers to the prohibition.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:11:1.hebrew: ה"ג דאמר ליה מדעתו - אם ארצה אחזירם, ולא שתתבעני בדין. הלכך מותר, דאי נמי חזר וקיבל מעותיו, עד עכשיו שלו היתה, וחוזר ומוכרה לו. אבל רישא, שע"כ צריך להחזיר, מעיקרא לאו מכר הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:11:1.english: This is the reading: Where he said to him, "of his own accord" - [Meaning:] "If I want, I will return them, and not that you may sue me in court." Therefore it is permitted, for even if [the buyer] went back and accepted his money, until now [the field] was his, and he sells it back to him. But in the first clause, where he is compelled to return [it], from the outset it is not a sale.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:12:1.hebrew: שלא באחריות - שאם יטרפנה בעל חוב שלי, לא אחזיר לך כלום. וכגון דפריש ליה הכי בהדיא בשטרא, דאי מסתמא, הא מוקמינא (לעיל בבא מציעא ד' טו:) כשמואל דאמר: אחריות טעות סופר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:12:1.english: Without a guarantee - [Meaning] that if my creditor seizes it, I will not return anything to you. And [this is] in a case where he stipulated this to him explicitly in the deed, for if [the sale were made] without specification, we have already established (above, Bava Metzia 15b) in accordance with Shmuel, who says [that the omission of] a guarantee is a scribal error.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:12:2.hebrew: מגבינא שופרא שבחא ופירי - מעידית שבנכסי אפרע לך, אף את השבח שתשביח והפירות שיטרפו ממך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:12:2.english: I will pay [from the] best[-quality], improvement, and produce - From the best-quality of my property I will pay you, even [for] the improvement that you will make and the produce that will be seized from you.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:1:1.hebrew: והלכתא כר' אלעזר - דרבית קצוצה יוצאה בדיינין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:1:1.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar - That fixed interest is reclaimed by the judges.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:2:1.hebrew: ה"ג במתניתין - מכר לו את השדה ונתן לו מקצת דמים, ואמר לו: אימתי שתרצה, הבא מותר המעות שעליך וטול שדה שלך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:2:1.english: This is how we read in the Mishnah - [If one] sold him the field and [the buyer] gave him part of the money, and [the seller] said to him: "Whenever you wish, bring the remainder of the money that you owe and take your field."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:2:2.hebrew: אסור - לעשות כן. ודוקא דאמר ליה: "לכי מייתית מותר המעות, קנה מעכשיו". לפיכך אסור לעשות כן: שאם יאכל מוכר פירות בתוך כך, לכשיביא זה המעות, נמצא שהשדה קנויה לו מיום המכר, וזה אכל הפירות בשכר המתנת מעותיו. ואם יאכל לוקח פירות מעכשיו, שמא לא יביא מותר המעות ויחזור לו זה מה שקיבל, ונמצא שלא היתה שדה קנויה לו — דהא "לכי מייתית קני מעכשיו" אמר ליה, והא לא אייתי — ומעות הראשונות כמלוה בעלמא היו אצל מוכר, וזה אכל פירות בשכרו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:2:2.english: [It is] prohibited - to do so. And [this is] specifically where [the seller] said to him: "When you bring the remainder of the money, acquire [it] from now." Therefore, it is prohibited to do so: for if the seller eats the produce in the meantime, when this [buyer] brings the money, it turns out that the field was acquired by him from the day of the sale, and this [seller] ate the produce as reward for waiting for his money. And if the buyer eats the produce from now, perhaps he will not bring the remainder of the money, and this [seller] will return to him what he received, and it turns out that the field was not acquired by him — for he said to him, "When you bring [it], acquire [it] from now," and he did not bring [it] — and the initial money was merely like a loan in the seller's possession, and this [buyer] ate the produce as its reward.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:1.hebrew: מי אוכל פירות - מכר וקבל מקצת, מי אוכל פירות בתוך כך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:1.english: Who eats the produce - [If one] sold [it] and received part [of the payment], who eats the produce in the meantime?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:2.hebrew: מוכר אוכל פירות - לקמיה מוקי שפיר, כדמפרש ולא פליגי כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:2.english: The seller enjoys the profits - Later on, [the Gemara] establishes [this] well, as it explains: "And they do not disagree," etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:3.hebrew: משלשין - מפקידין אותו ביד שליש. אם יגמור מקחו, יתנם ללוקח, ואם לא, יחזיר המוכר מה שקיבל ויטול פירותיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:3.english: They deposit [with a third party] - They deposit it in the hand of a third party. If [the buyer] completes his purchase, [the third party] gives them to the buyer; and if not, the seller returns what he received and takes his produce.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:4.hebrew: הא דאמר ליה לכי מייתית קני - מוכר אוכל פירות, שאין השדה קנויה לו אלא מכאן ולהבא, ועד השתא דידיה אכל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:4.english: This [refers to a case] where he said to him, "When you bring [the money], acquire [it]" - The seller consumes [the] produce, for the field is not acquired by him except from then onward, and until now, [it is] his own [that] he consumes.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:5.hebrew: הא דאמר לכי מייתית קני מעכשיו - אין זה אלא תנאי, שאם יקיים תנאו יהא השדה קנוי לו מן היום. ואם קיים תנאו, נמצא שאכל המוכר פירות של לוקח עד עכשיו בשכר המתנת מעותיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:3:5.english: That [case] where he says, "When you bring [the money], acquire [it] from now" - This is only a condition, that if he fulfills his condition, the field will be acquired by him from today. And if he fulfills his condition, it turns out that the seller consumed the buyer's produce until now as reward for waiting for his money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:4:1.hebrew: תני רב ספרא - ולא היה מפורש במשנה מתי שניהן מותרין ומתי אסורין, ופי' רבא מסברא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:4:1.english: Rav Safra taught - And it was not explicitly stated in the Mishnah when both are permitted and when [they] are prohibited, and Rava explained [it] through reasoning.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:5:1.hebrew: קני מהשתא כשיעור זוזך - והשאר לכי מייתית קני. זה אוכל פירות קרקע המגיע לדמים שנתן, והמוכר אוכל השאר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:5:1.english: Acquire from now according to the measure of your money - and the rest, when you bring [the money], acquire [it]. This one [the buyer] eats the produce of the land corresponding to the money that he gave, and the seller eats the rest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:5:2.hebrew: לכי מייתית קני - הכל מעכשיו, שניהם אסורין כדפרישית לעיל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:5:2.english: When you bring [the money], acquire - all of it from now: both of them are prohibited, as I explained above.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:6:1.hebrew: לכי מייתית קני - עד דמייתי, שדה של מוכר הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:6:1.english: When you bring [the money], acquire [it] - Until he brings [the money], the field belongs to the seller.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:6:2.hebrew: קני מעכשיו וזוזי ליהוו הלוואה גבך - כיון דאקנייה מעכשיו, הרי היא של לוקח; ואם יאכל מוכר פירות, בשכר המתנת מעות יאכלם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:6:2.english: Acquire [it] from now, and the money shall be a loan with you - Since he conveyed it to him from now, it belongs to the buyer; and if the seller consumes [the] produce, he consumes it as compensation for waiting for the money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:7:1.hebrew: צד אחד - דלמא אתי לידי רבית, דלמא לא אתי. כיצד? אם מוכר אוכלם ולא גמר לוקח מקחו, אין כאן רבית; גמר, יש כאן רבית. הלכך, דלא כרבי יהודה. אבל סיפא קתני מוכר מותר ולוקח אסור, לוקח מותר מוכר אסור — אפי' רבי יהודה מודה דהתם ודאי איכא רבית. דכי אמר ליה "לכי מייתית קני", אין לו עכשיו בה כלום ואפילו גמר; הלכך, פירי דהשתא רבית הן אצלו. והיכא דאמר ליה "קני מעכשיו וזוזי ניהוו הלוואה גבך", הרי קנויה לו מעכשיו, ואם יאכל מוכר פירות, הרי הוא רבית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:7:1.english: One side [of interest] - Perhaps it will come to interest, [and] perhaps it will not come [to interest]. How so? If the seller eats them [the produce] and the buyer does not complete his purchase, there is no interest here; [if] he completes [it], there is interest here. Therefore, [this is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda. However, [regarding] the latter clause [where] it teaches: "[If] the seller is permitted, then the buyer is prohibited; [if] the buyer is permitted, [then] the seller is prohibited" — even Rabbi Yehuda agrees that there, there is certainly interest. For when he says to him, "When you bring [the money], acquire [it]," [the buyer] has nothing in it now, even if he [eventually] completes [the purchase]; therefore, the produce of now is interest for him [the buyer, if he eats it]. And where he says to him, "Acquire [it] from now, and let the zuz be a loan with you," behold, it is acquired by him from now, and if the seller eats the produce, it is interest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:8:1.english: [If] one pledged a house to him - It is a baraita.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:8:2.english: For this money - [The lender] fixed a small sum for him to add to the loan money, to make it permanently his if [the borrower] comes to sell it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:9:1.hebrew: צד אחד - האי נמי, דלמא לא אתי לידי רבית, דלא ירצה למוכרה לעולם. ולרבי יהודה, אם ירצה למוכרה, מותר לזה לקבלה בדמים שפסק, דמתחילת התנאי צד אחד הוא דהוה ברבית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 65b:9:1.english: One side - This [case] too perhaps will not come to interest, for he might never wish to sell it. And according to Rabbi Yehuda, if he wishes to sell it, it is permitted for this [party] to take it for the price that he stipulated, since from the beginning of the condition it is [only] one side that involves interest.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 65b:10:1.hebrew: לכשיהיו לי מעות החזירם לי אסור - דלא כרבי יהודה. ולא דמי למשכנתא בלא נכייתא (לקמן בבא מציעא ד' סז:), דהכא אם לא יפדה אין זה מלוה אלא מכר; אבל משכנתא יכולים לעולם לפדות, או הוא או יורשיו, אבל כאן — נהי דהוא יכול לפדות, יורשיו אין יכולין לפדות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 65b:10:1.english: "When I have money, return them to me" — [it is] prohibited - [This is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda. And it is not similar to a mashkanta [pledge] without deduction (below, Bava Metzia 67b), because here, if he does not redeem [it], this is not a loan, rather a sale; whereas a mashkanta can always be redeemed, either by him or by his heirs, but here — granted that he can redeem [it], his heirs cannot redeem [it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 65b:1:1.hebrew: והלכתא כרב חמא - אור"ת דהלכתא נמי כר"נ בטרשא, מדקאמר לקמן (בבא מציעא דף סח.): "לית הלכתא כטרשא דפפונאי", מכלל דבהנך הוי הלכתא. והא דנקט הכא "הלכתא כרב חמא", לא אתא לאשמועינן אלא לאפוקי דרב פפא. והיינו טעמא: דר"נ לא שרי אלא בדלא קץ, אבל רב פפא ורב חמא איירו אפילו בקץ או כשהשער קבוע דהוי כקץ; ורב פפא אשינויא דרב נחמן קאי, ד"שאני הכא דקץ לה". ולא גרסי' במילתא דרב פפא "טרשא דידי ודאי שרי", דמשמע לישנא ד"ודאי" דיותר שרי מדרב נחמן, אלא גרסינן "טרשא דידי שרי". ואי גרס ליה, איכא למימר דלסברא דרב פפא דלא אזיל בתר לוקח שרי טפי; אבל לפי האמת, דרב נחמן שריא ודרב פפא אסור. וכן פסק רב האי גאון בשער מ"ב דהלכתא כטרשא דרב נחמן, אך פירש טרשא דר"נ בע"א ממה שאנו מפרשים:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 65b:1:1.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Rav Ḥama - Rabbeinu Tam says that the halakha is also in accordance with Rav Naḥman regarding tarsha [credit sale at a higher price], since [the Gemara] says later (Bava Metzia 68a): "The halakha is not in accordance with the tarsha of the Papuneans," which implies that in those [other cases] the halakha is [in accordance with them]. And the reason it stated here "the halakha is in accordance with Rav Ḥama" is only to teach us to exclude [the tarsha] of Rav Pappa. And this is the reason: Rav Naḥman only permits [it] when he did not fix [a price], whereas Rav Pappa and Rav Ḥama are speaking even where he fixed [a price], or when the market price is established, which is like fixing [a price]; and Rav Pappa is referring to Rav Naḥman's answer, [namely] that "here it is different because he fixed it for him." And we do not read in Rav Pappa's statement "my tarsha is certainly permitted," because the expression "certainly" implies that it is more permitted than Rav Naḥman's; rather, we read "my tarsha is permitted." And if one does read it, it can be said that according to Rav Pappa's own reasoning — that he does not follow the buyer — it is more permitted; however, according to the truth, Rav Naḥman's [tarsha] is permitted and Rav Pappa's is forbidden. And so too ruled Rav Hai Gaon in Gate 42, that the halakha is in accordance with the tarsha of Rav Naḥman, although he explained Rav Naḥman's tarsha differently from how we explain [it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 65b:3:1.hebrew: רב הונא אמר מוכר אוכל פירות כו' - ולא רצו לפרש "לוקח אוכל פירות", וכדאמר ליה "ארעא קנויה לך מעכשיו וזוזי ליהוי הלואה גבך" כדבסמוך; דאמתני' קיימי, דקתני: "הבא מעות וטול את שלך". ומשמע להו "וטול את שלך" — זכי את שלך וקני מקחך, דע"י הבאת מעות קני מעתה או למפרע; ולא משמע להו "טול את שלך" — שכבר קנית, אלא שבתורת משכון נשאר בידו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 65b:3:1.english: Rav Huna says: The seller enjoys the profits, etc. - And they [Rav Huna and Rav Anan] did not want to explain [that] the buyer enjoys the profits, [as in a case] where he says to him, "The land is acquired by you from now, and the money shall be a loan with you," as [the Gemara states] shortly below; for they are addressing the Mishnah, which teaches: "Bring the money and take yours." And "and take yours" means to them: acquire yours and take possession of your purchase, [indicating] that through bringing the money he acquires [it] from now or retroactively; and "take yours" does not mean to them that you have already acquired [it], and it merely remained in his [the seller's] possession as a pledge:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 65b:8:1.hebrew: לא תמכרם אלא לי בדמים הללו אסור - מה שפירש בקונטרס: פסק לו דמים מועטין להוסיף על מעות הללו להעמידה בידו אם בא למוכרה — משום דלאו אורחא דמילתא הוא שימחול לו לגמרי בדמי הלואה, דלמה יעשה כן? דטוב לו שתהא בתורת משכון שיפדה מתי שירצה. ובחנם פירש כן; דבלאו תוספת דמים פוסק עמו להצמיתה בידו אם בא למוכרה, דכשידחוק אותו מלוה ממעותיו ע"כ יהא זקוק לפדותה או למוכרה. וא"ת: אמאי אסרינן הכא? והא תנן לקמן (בבא מציעא ד' סה.): "הלוהו על שדהו וא"ל: אם אי אתה נותן לי מכאן ועד ג' שנים הרי היא שלי — הרי היא שלו", ומסתמא איירי בלוקח בפחות משויה; וכן משמע בגמרא (לקמן בבא מציעא סו.), דקאמר: "לאחר מתן מעות לא קנה אלא כנגד מעותיו". וי"ל: דלמאי דמוקי לה מעכשיו — א"ש, דלא הויא הלואה. ואפילו למאן דמוקי לה בלא מעכשיו, מ"מ התם הלוה היה יכול למכור מן השדה לאחר כנגד המלוה וליקח לעצמו המותר; וכשהוא מניח לו כולה, אינו עושה משום רבית, אלא מילתא בעלמא הוא דעבד (מלוה לגביה) שמחל לו בחנם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 65b:8:1.english: "Sell them only to me for this money" — it is prohibited - Regarding what Rashi explained — [namely, that] he stipulated with him a small [amount of] money to add to this money [of the loan] in order to establish it in his possession if he comes to sell it — [Rashi explained it this way] because it is not the way of things that [the borrower] would completely waive [the excess value] to him for the loan money; for why would he do so, when it is better for him that it remain in the status of a pledge that he may redeem whenever he wants? But he explained this needlessly; for even without an addition of money, he stipulates with him to transfer it permanently into his possession if he comes to sell it, because when the lender presses him for his money, he will perforce be compelled either to redeem it or to sell it. And if you ask: Why do we prohibit [this] here? Behold, we learned in a Mishnah below (Bava Metzia 65a): "If one lent him [money] against his field and said to him: 'If you do not give me [payment] from now until three years, it is mine,' it is his" — and presumably it is speaking of a case where he acquires [it] for less than its value; and so too it is implied in the Gemara (below, Bava Metzia 66a), where it says: "After the giving of the money, he only acquires [an amount] corresponding to his money." And one can answer: According to the one who establishes it [as taking effect] "from now," it works out well, for it is not a loan. And even according to the one who establishes it without "from now," nevertheless there the borrower could have sold [a portion] of the field to another [person] corresponding to the loan and taken the remainder for himself; and when he leaves the entire [field] to him, he is not doing [so] on account of interest, but rather it is merely a simple favor that he did (the lender toward him [i.e., the borrower toward the lender]) in that he waived [the excess] to him gratuitously.
